🏎️ ONE WEEK TO MONZA — AND THE STORYLINES ARE ABSOLUTELY STACKED 🏎️

The 2026 Italian Grand Prix (September 4-6 at Autodromo Nazionale di Monza) is one week away, and the buildup to Ferrari's home race has produced one of the most compelling pre-race narratives of the entire season.

Here's what you need to know:

🔴 KIMI ANTONELLI — The championship leader will start from the back of the grid after Mercedes completed a full power unit change, exceeding the season's allocation. Toto Wolff confirmed the penalty, with Monza notably being the best circuit on the calendar for recovery thanks to its slipstreaming opportunities and low-downforce characteristics.

🔴 FERRARI ADUO-2 — The Scuderia debuts its second major engine upgrade of 2026, expected to deliver approximately 15 additional horsepower and 0.2 seconds per lap at Monza — the most power-sensitive circuit in F1.

🔴 LEWIS HAMILTON — Currently 53 points behind Antonelli, this is Hamilton's clearest window to close the gap all season. Antonelli starting last + Ferrari running its best engine = a weekend where anything can happen.

11 races remain. The championship is not over. Monza is where the real fight begins.

Who do you think wins the 2026 Italian GP? 🇮🇹

facebook.long_form:
⚡ FERRARI'S ADUO-2: THE ENGINE UPGRADE THAT COULD CHANGE EVERYTHING ⚡

Ferrari has confirmed that its second major power unit upgrade of 2026 — internally designated ADUO-2 — will make its debut at the Italian Grand Prix at Monza.

Here are the details:

🔧 WHAT CHANGED: The upgrade centres on the turbocharger and combustion chamber. Ferrari has fitted a larger impeller to the turbocharger while redesigning the combustion architecture. The original 2026 Ferrari power unit was built with a smaller turbo to minimize lag — a benefit that disappeared when the FIA introduced a new five-second pre-start procedure, leaving Ferrari with a significant straight-line speed deficit.

🔧 HOW MUCH FASTER: Ferrari's simulations project approximately 15 additional horsepower. At Monza — the longest, fastest, most power-sensitive circuit in the championship — that translates to roughly 0.2 seconds per lap. Over 53 laps, that compounds significantly.

🔧 MERCEDES RESPONDS: Reports indicate Mercedes has been forced to accelerate its own upgrade timeline to counter the Ferrari threat at Monza.

🔧 THE TIMING: Kimi Antonelli starts from the back of the grid at this exact race. If Ferrari's ADUO-2 is as good as the simulations suggest, Hamilton could leave Monza with the championship picture dramatically changed.

How much do YOU think Ferrari's engine upgrade is worth this weekend? 👇

facebook.long_form:
⚖️ THREE MONTHS LATER — THE MONACO GP RESULT IS STILL NOT OFFICIAL ⚖️

The 2026 Monaco Grand Prix was run on June 7. Today is August 28 — and F1 fans still don't know the final, official podium.

Here's where things stand:

During the race, six drivers across five teams received pit-lane speeding penalties. Pierre Gasly of Alpine received two five-second penalties — dropping him from P3 to P7. But the FIA subsequently acknowledged that the pit-lane speed limit had been incorrectly calculated due to a measurement error by Formula One Management.

Gasly successfully appealed and was restored to P3. Isack Hadjar was demoted to P4. Oscar Piastri was demoted to P5.

Red Bull and McLaren — whose drivers were pushed down in the standings — appealed Gasly's reinstatement. The FIA International Court of Appeal heard those arguments in Paris on August 25.

The verdict? Could take up to three weeks. That means the final Monaco GP result might not be confirmed until mid-September.

In the meantime: the points for Gasly, Hadjar, Piastri — and everyone around them — remain provisional.

Is this the most complicated race result in modern F1 history? 👇

facebook.long_form:
🏆 LANDO NORRIS WINS IN ZANDVOORT — TWO IN A ROW 🏆

Lando Norris won the Dutch Grand Prix at Circuit Zandvoort on Sunday, crossing the line 11.5 seconds ahead of championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second consecutive race victory.

The race began in dramatic fashion when Max Verstappen lost the rear of his Red Bull on lap 1 and hit the barriers heavily, triggering a red flag restart. Verstappen's home crowd watched in silence as their favourite retired before the race had barely begun.

From the restart, Norris was in total control. Antonelli finished second, George Russell third.

The results: Norris now sits 83 points behind Antonelli in the championship with 11 races remaining — and with Antonelli facing a grid penalty at Monza next weekend, the reigning champion is seeing his window open just a little wider.

Can Norris make it three wins in a row at Monza? 🤔
